passages: September 10, 2026: Today, Governor Gavin Newsom signed into law Senate Bill 1119, Adam's Law.

The release lists risk assessments, crisis support, parent-controlled default settings, limits on harmful outputs, incident reporting, advertising limits and independent audits among the law's requirements.
records.limitation: This is an official release from a bill author and contains advocacy claims about strength and expected effectiveness. It confirms signing; the enrolled text governs precise requirements and dates.

records.authority: Primary enrolled bill text for definitions, duties, operative dates and audit exceptions.
records.accessObservation: The enrolled text was reopened from the preserved September 11 retrieval.
passages: Section 21812 requires a documented child-safety risk assessment before a new or substantially modified companion chatbot is made available in California and documented reasonable mitigation of identified risks.

For operators permitting child users, Section 21812 requires crisis-response protocols, age-appropriate notices, parent-controlled defaults that disable push notifications and ordinarily disable persistent conversational memory, and limits of one continuous hour and two total hours per day.
The persistent-memory default contains a qualified exception for users 16 or older when specified guardrails are implemented.

Section 21812 requires reasonable measures against listed behaviors including encouraging self-harm, sexual material, romantic interest, claims of sentience, emotional reliance, disproportionate praise and instructions to evade parental controls.
Section 21814 sets an initial child-safety audit deadline of January 1, 2029 or before first public availability, whichever is later, with later audits generally every two years.
Before January 1, 2032, the audit section does not apply to an operator with less than $500 million in prior-calendar-year gross revenue.

The enrolled text was dated September 8 and the preserved status/history pages still showed presented to the Governor on September 9 when checked; those lagging pages do not negate the later official signing confirmation.
records.limitation: This is enrolled statutory text, not legal advice or proof that implementation will prevent harm. Exceptions and cross-references matter; the candidate reports only the cited high-level provisions.

passages: AP reported that Newsom signed the child online-safety package on September 10, including the companion-chatbot safety law.
AP reported that the chatbot law was inspired by Adam Raine's story and quoted Maria Raine on parents' need to understand AI-companion risks.
records.limitation: AP confirms the event and context. It does not replace the statutory text or prove the safeguards' future effectiveness.

sourceBoundary.verified: Official sponsor confirmation and AP independently support the September 10 signing; the enrolled text supports the cited duties, dates and audit exception.
sourceBoundary.notVerified: No claim is made that controls started on signing, that every chatbot or operator is covered identically, that audits begin immediately, or that the law guarantees safety.
sourceBoundary.statusLag: The legislative status/history pages still lagged at presented to Governor during the check; they are preserved as a timing discrepancy, not treated as veto evidence.
